masthead.kicker: Hidden Champions of India / a DeepThought series

headline.text: Miven Mayfran Conveyors: a real Tsubakimoto-backed JV, currently shrinking.

subhead.text: A 1986 Hubli joint venture with a genuine global chip-conveyor leader — Mayfran International, owned by Japan's Tsubakimoto Chain since 2012 — whose India revenue and returns are both currently declining.

snapshot.label: Revenue
snapshot.value: ₹61.57 Cr FY25 (₹50-100 Cr band), down ~8% YoY

snapshot.label: JV structure
snapshot.value: JV with Mayfran International (USA) via Mayfran International B.V. (Netherlands) and the Sirur family (Hubli); Mayfran itself part of Tsubakimoto Chain Group (Japan) since 2012

p1_engine.eyebrow: A real global JV, currently on a down cycle

blocks.text: Revenue was ₹61.57 Cr in FY25, down roughly 8% YoY, with both ROE (-1.08%) and ROCE (-6.46%) negative — a genuinely soft year across the board. Net margin is barely positive at 0.56%. EBITDA growth had been strongly positive in an earlier filing year (+74.57% YoY, FY23), so the current decline reads as a recent reversal rather than a chronic pattern, though the most recent data point is the negative one.

It describes itself as a pioneer in India for chip, scrap, and coolant management systems, offering a comprehensive portfolio of solutions — a self-claimed positioning the HVT sheet itself flags `needs_verify: yes`.

What is independently confirmed, not just self-claimed: this is a genuine, structural joint venture with Mayfran International (through its subsidiary Mayfran International B.V. of the Netherlands) and the Sirur family of Hubli — and since 2012, Mayfran International itself has been part of Japan's Tsubakimoto Chain Group. Corporate records show nominee directors tied to both JV partners, confirming a real equity-and-technology relationship, not just co-branding.

It holds ISO 9001:2008 certification and lists Toyota, Bosch, Mahindra, and Maruti Suzuki as customers (undated, company-claimed). It markets itself as globally networked via Mayfran International (USA) and Mayfran International B.V. (Netherlands), though specific export countries or export-revenue percentage were not found.

insights.point: A market with **real structural tailwinds from manufacturing automation**, though India-specific sizing wasn't found.
insights.evidence: Global chip conveyor market: $1,322M (2024) to $1,818M by 2031 (~4.6%/yr); global coolant filtration systems market: $2.9B (2025) to $7.3B by 2036 (8.7%/yr), with semiconductor fab expansion cited as a specific driver.

insights.point: **Mayfran International is a genuine top-5 global player**, not a marginal brand — this is a real credibility anchor for the India JV.
insights.evidence: Hennig, Mayfran International, Jorgensen Conveyors (LNS Group), KNOLL Maschinenbau, and PRAB together hold ~38.5% of global chip conveyor market revenue; Mayfran's parent Tsubakimoto Chain posted ¥279.19B group revenue in FY2024, +4.64% YoY.

insights.point: **OEM design-stage bundling** is the segment's structural pattern — chip/coolant vendors increasingly integrate with machine-tool builders at the design stage.
insights.evidence: KNOLL Maschinenbau's integration with major German machine-tool OEMs (DMG Mori, Trumpf, Gildemeister) illustrates the pattern; Miven Mayfran's own customer list (Toyota, Bosch, Mahindra, Maruti Suzuki) suggests similar OEM-embedded relationships domestically.

reflect.text: The JV backing here is real and independently confirmed — a genuine top-5 global player's India arm, not a paper partnership. That makes the current revenue decline and negative returns more of a cyclical question than an identity one: does this reflect a broader India machine-tool capex slowdown, or something specific to Miven Mayfran's own execution?

p3_opportunities.lede: One clear place worth watching, named directly in the company's own gap research — with a real financial caveat attached.

items.title: Extending beyond core waste-to-value transformation into new revenue streams
items.body: The HVT sheet's own gap research names untapped potential to create new revenue streams beyond current chip/coolant waste transformation — but given the current -8% revenue decline and negative returns, this reads as a longer-horizon opportunity contingent on first understanding why the core business softened this year.
items.source: HVT gap research (marketintelo.com chip conveyor market report).

guesslabel.text: Possibilities, not prescriptions — and the honest first step here is diagnosing this year's revenue decline before pursuing new revenue streams.

items.title: Separate cyclical (machine-tool capex) softness from company-specific execution
items.body: Check whether India's broader machine-tool industry capex softened in the same period (a sector-wide check, per established methodology) before treating the -8% revenue and negative ROE/ROCE as company-specific weakness — the strong Mayfran/Tsubakimoto backing suggests this is worth diagnosing rather than assuming.
